manifest.name: OpenSSF Best Practices Badge (CII)
manifest.author: OpenSSF (Packaged by ComplianceOS)
manifest.description: The OpenSSF Best Practices Badge (formerly CII Best Practices) is a set of best practices for Free/Libre and Open Source Software (FLOSS) projects to show that they follow security and quality standards.

phases.name: V1: Basics
phases.description: Fundamental requirements for project transparency, licensing, and documentation.

phases.name: V2: Change Control
phases.description: Requirements for version control, release management, and change tracking.

phases.name: V3: Reporting
phases.description: Processes for handling bug reports and security vulnerabilities.

phases.name: V4: Quality
phases.description: Requirements for build quality, testing, and code health.

phases.name: V5: Security
phases.description: Specific security practices including cryptography and memory safety.

phases.name: V6: Analysis
phases.description: Use of automated tools to analyze code quality and security.

requirements.title: Project Website
requirements.description: Verify that the project has a website that describes what the software does and how to get it.

requirements.title: Contribution Information
requirements.description: Verify that the project provides clear information on how to contribute and the contribution process.

requirements.title: FLOSS License
requirements.description: Verify that the software is released as FLOSS (Free/Libre and Open Source Software) with an OSI-approved license.

requirements.title: Documentation
requirements.description: Verify that the project provides basic documentation on how to install and use the software.

requirements.title: Secure Sites (HTTPS)
requirements.description: Verify that the project sites (website, repository, download URLs) support HTTPS using TLS.

requirements.title: Discussion Mechanisms
requirements.description: Verify that the project has a mechanism for discussion (mailing list, forum, issue tracker) that is searchable and accessible.

requirements.title: Public Version Control
requirements.description: Verify that the project uses a publicly readable version-controlled source repository (e.g., git).

requirements.title: Unique Versioning
requirements.description: Verify that project results have a unique version identifier for each release.

requirements.title: Semantic Versioning
requirements.description: Verify that the project uses a standard version numbering format (e.g., Semantic Versioning or CalVer).

requirements.title: Release Tags
requirements.description: Verify that each release is identified within the version control system (e.g., using git tags).

requirements.title: Release Notes
requirements.description: Verify that release notes are provided for each release, summarizing major changes.

requirements.title: Vulnerability Identification
requirements.description: Verify that release notes identify any fixed vulnerabilities.

requirements.title: Bug Reporting Process
requirements.description: Verify that the project provides a process for users to submit bug reports.

requirements.title: Issue Tracker
requirements.description: Verify that the project uses an issue tracker to track individual issues.

requirements.title: Bug Response
requirements.description: Verify that the project acknowledges a majority of bug reports submitted in the last 2-12 months.

requirements.title: Vulnerability Reporting
requirements.description: Verify that the project has a documented process for reporting security vulnerabilities.

requirements.title: Private Vulnerability Reporting
requirements.description: Verify that the vulnerability reporting process supports private reports (e.g., via email or encrypted channel).

requirements.title: Vulnerability Response SLA
requirements.description: Verify that the project responds to vulnerability reports within 14 days.

requirements.title: Working Build
requirements.description: Verify that the project can be built using standard tools.

requirements.title: Automated Test Suite
requirements.description: Verify that the project has an automated test suite.

requirements.title: New Test Policy
requirements.description: Verify that new features or bug fixes typically include new tests.

requirements.title: Warning Flags
requirements.description: Verify that compiler/linter warning flags are enabled and addressed.

requirements.title: Test Invocation
requirements.description: Verify that there is a standard way to run the tests (e.g., 'npm test', 'make test').

requirements.title: Secure Development Knowledge
requirements.description: Verify that at least one primary developer knows how to design secure software.

requirements.title: Good Cryptography
requirements.description: Verify that if the project uses cryptography, it uses standard, publicly vetted algorithms and protocols.

requirements.title: No Leaked Secrets
requirements.description: Verify that the repository does not contain leaked private credentials or secrets.

requirements.title: No Broken Algorithms
requirements.description: Verify that the project avoids using known broken or weak cryptographic algorithms (e.g., MD5, SHA1 for security).

requirements.title: Secure Delivery
requirements.description: Verify that the software is distributed using secure channels (HTTPS).

requirements.title: Static Code Analysis
requirements.description: Verify that the project uses at least one static code analysis tool (linter, SAST) to detect common errors.

requirements.title: Dynamic Analysis
requirements.description: Verify that the project uses dynamic analysis tools (e.g., fuzzing) if appropriate for the language/type.
